summary: Static architecture combining Astro frontend and serverless/static backend with no database hosted on Netlify (Free). Estimated monthly infrastructure cost ranges from $0 to $0.

frontend.justification: Content-first static site generation with islands architecture minimizes client-side JavaScript, maximizing SEO and read-heavy performance.

alternatives.why_not: Heavier client runtime than needed for purely markdown-driven content.

tradeoffs: Complex stateful interactivity requires islands hydration.

backend.justification: Read-heavy content and markdown pages are fully pre-rendered at build time; dynamic backend server is unnecessary.

alternatives.why_not: Running a persistent server adds unnecessary operational overhead and cost for static content.
Massive over-engineering trap: decomposing a read-heavy content site into microservices introduces distributed latency and operational burden without any functional benefit.

tradeoffs: Forms and interactive inputs require external serverless handler or webhook.

database.justification: Content site relies on static Markdown files; persistent database server is not required.

alternatives.why_not: Adds unneeded infrastructure cost ($15+/mo) and maintenance for static read-only articles.

tradeoffs: Dynamic user-generated comments or profiles require external service.

hosting.justification: Global edge CDN hosting with automated Git deployments and edge caching, serving pre-rendered static assets with zero compute overhead.

alternatives.why_not: Massive over-engineering trap: running container orchestration for pre-rendered content incurs extreme cost ($70+/mo minimum) and unnecessary operational complexity.
Running dedicated container compute for static read-only files is redundant when assets can be served directly from global edge caches.

tradeoffs: Monthly build minutes and bandwidth caps on free/entry tiers; dynamic backend logic requires external serverless handlers.

supporting.justification: Serverless form handling embedded in static HTML without deploying an application server.

alternatives.why_not: Netlify Forms is natively bundled with the hosting provider.

tradeoffs: 100 submissions per month limit on free tier.

assumptions: Estimates based on published cloud pricing units and standard resource allocations.
Operating within generous free-tier limits (e.g. Netlify/Vercel static hosting).
